points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 罗莎·卢森堡出生于波兰扎莫希奇的一个犹太商人家庭，在华沙成长。她从小就展现出非凡的智力，尽管当时波兰处于俄国统治下，女性高等教育机会有限，但她通过参加地下大学课程接受了教育。1889年，因参与革命活动被迫离开波兰，前往瑞士，开始了她的流亡生活。这段经历奠定了她对民族自决和社会主义理论的早期思考。
points.descriptionEn: Rosa Luxemburg was born to a Jewish merchant family in Zamość, Poland, and grew up in Warsaw. From an early age, she demonstrated exceptional intelligence. Despite limited educational opportunities for women under Russian rule in Poland, she received education through underground university courses. In 1889, she was forced to leave Poland due to revolutionary activities and went into exile in Switzerland, beginning her life as an émigré. This period laid the foundation for her early thoughts on national self-determination and socialist theory.

points.title: 学术研究
points.description: 在苏黎世大学，卢森堡专注于经济学、法学和政治学的研究，获得了博士学位。她深入研究了资本主义经济危机理论，发展了关于帝国主义的理论，并撰写了重要著作《资本的积累》。在此期间，她积极参与波兰和德国社会民主党的活动，与列宁等人建立了联系，同时形成了自己独特的马克思主义观点，强调群众自发性革命行动的重要性，反对过于集中的政党控制。
points.descriptionEn: At the University of Zurich, Luxemburg focused on studying economics, law, and political science, earning her doctorate. She conducted in-depth research on capitalist economic crisis theory, developed theories on imperialism, and wrote her important work 'The Accumulation of Capital.' During this time, she actively participated in the activities of the Polish and German Social Democratic parties, established connections with figures like Lenin, and formed her unique Marxist perspective that emphasized the importance of spontaneous revolutionary action by the masses, opposing overly centralized party control.

points.title: 德国革命家
points.description: 卢森堡移居德国后，成为德国社会民主党(SPD)的重要理论家和批评者。她一方面肯定该党的成就，另一方面严厉批评其改良主义倾向和第一次世界大战中的支持立场。1906年，她因政治活动多次被捕入狱。在此期间，她撰写了《社会改良还是革命？》等重要著作，发展了关于群众罢工和革命的理论。1914年，当SPD支持战争拨款时，她与卡尔·李卜克内西等人一起创立了斯巴达克斯联盟，反对帝国主义战争。
points.descriptionEn: After moving to Germany, Luxemburg became an important theorist and critic within the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD). While acknowledging the party's achievements, she severely criticized its reformist tendencies and support for World War I. In 1906, she was arrested multiple times for political activities. During this period, she wrote important works like 'Reform or Revolution?' and developed theories on mass strikes and revolution. In 1914, when the SPD voted for war credits, she, along with Karl Liebknecht, founded the Spartacus League to oppose the imperialist war.

points.title: 战争与革命
points.description: 第一次世界大战期间，卢森堡因反战活动多次被捕入狱，在监狱中继续写作。1917年俄国革命后，她既支持布尔什维克推翻沙皇制度，又批评其建立一党专政和压制民主的做法。1918年德国十一月革命爆发后，她获释并积极参与革命活动，与卡尔·李卜克内西共同领导了斯巴达克斯联盟，后改组为德国共产党(KPD)。她主张建立社会主义民主共和国，反对暴力专政，强调保持民主自由的重要性。
points.descriptionEn: During World War I, Luxemburg was repeatedly imprisoned for anti-war activities but continued writing in prison. Following the 1917 Russian Revolution, she supported the Bolsheviks' overthrow of the tsarist system but criticized their establishment of one-party rule and suppression of democracy. When the German November Revolution broke out in 1918, she was released and actively participated in revolutionary activities, co-leading the Spartacus League with Karl Liebknecht, which was later reorganized into the Communist Party of Germany (KPD). She advocated for a socialist democratic republic, opposing violent dictatorship and emphasizing the importance of maintaining democratic freedoms.

points.title: 遇害与遗产
points.description: 1919年1月，卢森堡参与领导了柏林的斯巴达克斯起义，反对艾伯特政府的右翼政策。起义失败后，她于1月15日被捕，当天即被右翼民兵杀害，尸体被扔在兰德韦尔运河中。她的遇害成为德国革命史上的悲剧性事件，也使她成为国际社会主义运动的象征。她的著作和思想对后来的马克思主义理论、西方马克思主义和左翼政治思想产生了深远影响，至今仍被广泛研究和讨论。
points.descriptionEn: In January 1919, Luxemburg participated in leading the Spartacist uprising in Berlin against the right-wing policies of the Ebert government. After the uprising failed, she was arrested on January 15 and murdered the same day by right-wing militia, with her body thrown into the Landwehr Canal. Her assassination became a tragic event in German revolutionary history and made her a symbol of the international socialist movement. Her writings and ideas have had a profound impact on later Marxist theory, Western Marxism, and left-wing political thought, and continue to be widely studied and discussed today.

supporter.zh: 支持者视罗莎·卢森堡为社会主义理论家和革命先驱，她的思想融合了马克思主义的革命性与对民主自由的坚持。她强调群众自发性行动的重要性，反对官僚主义和教条主义，为后来的西方马克思主义奠定了基础。她的勇气和原则性在反对帝国主义战争和资本主义剥削的斗争中熠熠生辉，成为国际社会主义运动的永恒象征。
supporter.en: Supporters view Rosa Luxemburg as a socialist theorist and revolutionary pioneer whose ideas combined Marxist revolutionary principles with a commitment to democratic freedoms. She emphasized the importance of spontaneous mass action, opposing bureaucracy and dogmatism, laying the foundation for later Western Marxism. Her courage and principled stance in opposing imperialist war and capitalist exploitation shine brightly, making her an eternal symbol of the international socialist movement.

critic.zh: 批评者认为卢森堡的理论存在矛盾，她既强调群众自发性又主张集中领导，既批评列宁的集中制又未能提出可行的替代方案。她的革命策略在德国的失败表明理论与实践的脱节。此外，她对民族自决的绝对支持有时被视为忽视了现实政治复杂性，她的激进立场也未能有效应对20世纪初欧洲的社会变革挑战。
critic.en: Critics argue that Luxemburg's theories contained contradictions, as she emphasized both spontaneous mass action and centralized leadership, criticized Lenin's centralism without offering viable alternatives, and failed to bridge the gap between theory and practice as evidenced by the failure of her revolutionary strategy in Germany. Additionally, her absolute support for national self-determination is sometimes seen as ignoring the complexities of realpolitik, and her radical positions failed to effectively address the challenges of early 20th-century European social transformations.

objective.zh: 历史学界将卢森堡视为复杂的马克思主义思想家，她的理论贡献与局限并存。在流行文化中，她常被描绘为反抗不公的勇敢女性形象，代表知识分子的政治参与。她的著作《资本的积累》和《社会改良还是革命？》成为马克思主义经典，而她的悲剧性死亡使她成为革命浪漫主义的象征。当代学者更关注她对民主与社会主义关系的思考，以及她对生态危机的早期预见。
objective.en: Historiography views Luxemburg as a complex Marxist thinker whose theoretical contributions and limitations coexist. In popular culture, she is often depicted as a courageous woman resisting injustice, representing political engagement by intellectuals. Her works 'The Accumulation of Capital' and 'Reform or Revolution?' have become Marxist classics, and her tragic death has made her a symbol of revolutionary romanticism. Contemporary scholars focus more on her thoughts on the relationship between democracy and socialism, as well as her early predictions about ecological crises.

self.zh: 自由始终是自由者的特权，对于不自由者来说，它永远只是一个口号。
self.en: Freedom is always and exclusively freedom for the one who thinks differently.

others.zh: 罗莎·卢森堡是鹰，不是夜莺。她用锐利的目光观察世界，用尖锐的语言表达思想，她的生命和思想都充满了力量。
others.en: Rosa Luxemburg was an eagle, not a nightingale. She observed the world with sharp eyes and expressed her thoughts with sharp words; her life and thought were full of strength.
